headline: Nothing on sale: BTC $85.2K on a $648M short squeeze while the 10-year yield sits at 5%
summary: There is no dip to buy right now - all three majors are at or near the top of their day range. Bitcoin ran from an $81,164 open to an $85,438 intraday high, its first print above $85,000 since January, and trades around $85,242 (+5.7% in 24h), with ETH at about $2,726 (+5.5%) and SOL at about $118 (+9.3%). The fuel was forced short covering, not spot demand: $746.6m of positions were liquidated in 24 hours, $647.9m of it shorts (86% of the total, and roughly 96% in the peak hour), triggered by bitcoin's first weekly close above its 50-week average in 45 weeks and a fourth straight down session in Brent as Washington-Tehran diplomacy plays out at the UN. Open interest still rose 7.59% to about $156bn through the squeeze, so traders are replacing positions rather than capitulating. The macro behind it has not improved - the 10-year Treasury yield is at 5.00-5.04%, its highest since 2007, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said today that rates may have to go up 'more aggressively and more front-loaded' if inflation turns out to be demand-driven, and October hike odds sit around 50-60%. Sentiment is Greed (composite 64.5, Fear & Greed 70, BTC +9.8% / ETH +9.2% / SOL +15.3% on the week) while the 24h news tone stays negative at -0.73; this is a chase-or-wait tape, not a bounce setup.

BTC.note: Around $85,242 after covering its entire $80,394-$85,438 day range and reclaiming the $82,225 average cost basis of US spot ETF buyers for the first time since January; Hyperliquid funding is a modest 0.0016%/h (~0.04%/day) on $3.82bn open interest, so the squeeze has not yet built crowded long financing.

ETH.note: Around $2,726 and +9.2% on the week with roughly $59m of ether shorts liquidated in the peak hour, but it has the weakest fund sponsorship of the three - US spot ether ETFs snapped a four-week inflow streak in the week to 18 September - even as Bitmine added 27,562 ETH at $2,727 (~$75m).

SOL.note: Around $118 and the strongest of the three at +9.3% on the day and +15.3% on the week, carrying the highest futures premium (0.094%) and funding of 0.0023%/h on a much smaller $720m Hyperliquid book, with Alpenglow mainnet activation on 28 September as asset-specific event risk.

drivers.title: This is a short squeeze, not new money
drivers.detail: $746.6m of crypto positions were liquidated in 24 hours, of which $647.9m were shorts - 86% of the total, and about 96% in the peak hour ($226m bitcoin, $59m ether) across roughly 135,000 traders. The trigger was bitcoin's first weekly close above its 50-week moving average in 45 weeks; crucially, aggregate open interest still rose 7.59% to about $156bn during the squeeze, meaning positions are being replaced rather than closed out, which leaves the tape exposed to a reversal in the other direction.

drivers.title: The 10-year is at 5% and Goolsbee hardened the hiking message
drivers.detail: Speaking in London today, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said supply shocks 'have come more frequently, hit harder and lasted longer', that US inflation may now be demand-driven as well, and that in that case 'the rate response is more aggressive and more front-loaded' - with 'no ambiguity' about the need for higher rates. This follows the FOMC's 12-0 vote on 16 September to raise the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, the first hike in over three years and the first under Chair Kevin Warsh; the 10-year Treasury yield has since touched 5.00-5.04%, its highest since 2007, and October hike odds sit around 50-60%. The stored history flags this exact channel: 'inflation/CPI' headlines preceded a BTC dip within 6h 2.6% of the time versus 1.0% by chance (2.67x lift, n=117).

drivers.title: Today's bid is borrowed from oil, and the war is not settled
drivers.detail: Brent fell for a fourth consecutive session - its longest losing run in three months - on hopes that UN General Assembly diplomacy can defuse the US-Iran conflict, and that is what lifted S&P 500 futures more than 0.5%, Nasdaq 100 futures nearly 1%, and crypto alongside them. But the June memorandum of understanding is effectively defunct after Iranian strikes on shipping in July, the Strait of Hormuz dispute is unresolved, and Iranian President Pezeshkian only speaks at the UNGA on Tuesday - so the risk premium crypto is currently not paying can be reinstated by a single headline.

drivers.title: Treasury companies bought below spot; the passive bid did not
drivers.detail: Strategy filed an 8-K at 12:00 UTC today disclosing 950 BTC for about $76m bought between 14 and 20 September - its first purchase in weeks - alongside a $174m STRC repurchase, while Strive added 1,355 BTC for $107.7m and Bitmine bought 27,562 ETH at $2,727. By contrast, US spot bitcoin ETFs netted just $6.2m for the whole week to 18 September, salvaged by a $433m Friday, with IBIT taking $121m (cumulative $64.12bn) and FBTC $79.9m against a $142m ARKB outflow; spot ether funds snapped a four-week inflow streak. Corporate buying happened at or under today's price, not chasing it.

drivers.title: Washington sells the stablecoin story while yields say otherwise
drivers.detail: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent today defended the US economy by pointing to the dollar's role in 89.2% of FX transactions, the spread of dollar-pegged stablecoins, record median household income and the Atlanta Fed's 5.1% annualised Q3 GDP estimate, and said Treasury buybacks are about liquidity rather than suppressing yields - remarks delivered with the 10-year at 5%. He also framed Saudi Arabia's exit from the China-backed mBridge platform as a win for the dollar. Supportive rhetoric for stablecoin rails, but it is commentary, not flow.

drivers.title: Rulemaking replaces legislation; the ECB moves on tokenisation
drivers.detail: With the CLARITY Act dead on a 49-50 cloture vote on 15 September, the SEC and CFTC are writing US market-structure rules under existing authority, and the SEC's conditional five-year exemption window for tokenised-securities pilots opens tomorrow, 22 September. In parallel the ECB announced today that the Eurosystem will bring central bank money to tokenised finance via Pontes and that it will invest part of its own funds in tokenised securities. This is plumbing that lowers tail risk over time; it does not bid spot this week.

watch.what: Iranian President Pezeshkian addresses the UN General Assembly - the biggest single headline risk to the falling-oil bid holding up today's tape. The SEC's tokenised-securities exemption window also opens, TON unlocks about 1.3% of supply (~$51.2m), and Messari Mainnet NYC runs 22-24 September.
Xi Jinping arrives in the United States ahead of the summit; Humanity unlocks 14.7% of supply (~$20.8m).

US initial jobless claims for the week to 19 September, consensus 201K versus 196K prior - the first labour read since the hike, and the data channel that historically preceded BTC dips at 2.7x the base rate. Trump hosts Xi at the White House the same day.

Deribit quarterly BTC and ETH options expiry, around $16.6bn notional - the week's largest mechanical volatility source. Plasma (XPL) also unlocks roughly 1.76-1.81bn tokens (~63-65% of circulating supply, ~$158m). US durable goods orders land 12:30 UTC.
US PCE inflation - the single most important print of the week for the demand-driven-inflation question Goolsbee raised today, and therefore for October hike pricing.
Solana's Alpenglow mainnet activation, the largest protocol change of the quarter for SOL, following the 18 September cut in block time to 250ms. Q3 and the SEC fiscal year both end on 30 September.

Context for any pullback that does appear: the stored history says BTC dips during greed recovered +1.5% in 7 of 7 cases, ETH 92.9% of 28 and SOL 93.8% of 48, with a typical extra drop after the trigger of -0.3% to -0.5% and median time to recovery of 3.5-5.0 hours. Against that, today's market state most resembles 2025-07-10, 2025-06-10 and 2024-07-22, after which BTC's median 30-day move was -3.0% (up in 50.0% of them).
